svg.title: Here is the precise coalescence argument that uses it. Suppose a ghost P has all length compo- nents below k zero. Fix x ̸= y and a hosted product Q = Qn−1 i=0 Vi of total length k. Place P at x and Vi at y + tie0, for t > 0 sufficiently small. These points are distinct and avoid x. Expand all polynomials into monomials and apply Wick’s rule. A monomial of P of length l > k has too many letters to pair with the k exterior letters: it has no internal pair at x, so its moment is exactly zero. If l = k, every exterior letter must pair with a letter at x, leaving no exterior-to-exterior pair. All the resulting kernel arguments approach the nonzero vector x −y; their finite products therefore
